verdict: partly consistent: 80 signs = 80 letters, 23 groups = 23 words once read from the cipher (يدري ما به حكما; يقضي في ما علما); 97.4% / 97.4% over 76 repeated occurrences; the only breaks are in ك: the abraded ك of وحاكم is drawn like the ل cup, the ك of ضميرك like the ص U-hook, and the ك of حكما has a shape of its own A second by-eye pass distinguishes the two kaf forms by the double tooth and gives 76/76. Both passes agree on every letter.
notes: Rows 5-10 of image 0084_0115: 11 + 13 + 13 + 13 + 15 + 15 = 80 by eye (the record's 82 and 13-14 per row are the segmenter's). Both verses are enciphered here; the second is written out on 56r l.1.

Read from the cipher: يدري ما به حكما (groups ما | به: the ε-comb م and ٢ ا, then the L-hook ب and U ه), not the record's كمابه [?] (the clear text has كما به); and يقضي في ما علما (فيما, groups في | ما): the record's سما has no س in the cipher; the 2-sign group is the م sign and ا (cmp_a.png panel sama_s against alma_m).
A scraped patch on l.6 between صادقة's first two signs is not counted. The ك of وحاكم is partly abraded; what remains is the ل cup (cmp_km.png).

shape_recheck.agreement: Both transcriptions count 80 signs, give identical letters at every aligned position, and recover the same 23 word groups.

alternative.shape_evidence: The abraded bowl appears continuous below a short double tooth on the right. The two lam instances have a separate upper bar and long foot.
A simple rising left stroke and double right end distinguish this shape from the double left head and short right end in صادقة.

shape_recheck.interpretation: The more conservative classification is tabulated. Distinguishing the two kaf forms by the side of the double tooth removes both exceptions. Abrasion on line 6 limits the distinction.
